nodes.content: Reconstruct sparse-view 3D geometry with calibrated uncertainty distinguishing unobserved structure from ambiguities caused by reflective surfaces.
requirements: Achieve 85–95% coverage for nominal 90% surface-depth intervals, separately on occluded and reflective regions.
Reduce mean interval width by 20% versus a calibrated ensemble at matched observed-surface reconstruction error.

nodes.content: Build VisBRDF-SDF, a visibility-conditioned neural SDF posterior with view-dependent reflectance and separately calibrated occluded and reflective depth intervals.
Can VisBRDF-SDF distinguish reflection-induced depth ambiguity from unobserved geometry when reflective surfaces partially occlude the same ray?
Visibility and specular-residual factors will distinguish mixed-ray ambiguities with 85–95% coverage per region and 20% narrower intervals than calibrated ensembles.
Create MirrorOcclude-3V mixed-ray scenes; ablate visibility/specular factors, then calibrate intervals and compare regionwise coverage and width against matched-error ensembles.
Fit held-out regional calibrators; run five-seed MirrorOcclude-3V visibility/specular ablations against error-matched ensembles, measuring 90% depth coverage and width.
On five-seed MirrorOcclude-3V, VisBRDF-SDF achieved 91% occluded but 81% reflective coverage; intervals were 12% narrower than error-matched ensembles.
Separating specular-ray modes from occlusion priors should yield 85–95% coverage regionwise and ≥20% narrower intervals than matched-error ensembles.
Use n7's reflective failures to fit specular-ray mixture heads; compare regional coverage and width against matched-error ensembles on held-out MirrorOcclude-3V.
Held-out MirrorOcclude-3V: mixture heads achieved 90% occluded and 88% reflective coverage, with 23% narrower intervals than matched-error ensembles.
Adopt specular-ray mixture heads over original model: reflective coverage improved from 81% to 88%; intervals narrowed 23% versus ensembles.
Stratify MirrorOcclude-3V ablation predictions by mixed versus pure rays, measuring 90% interval coverage and width for each factor.
MirrorOcclude-3V ablation report with mixed/pure-ray 90% depth-interval coverage and mean width for visibility-only, specular-only, and joint variants.
How do visibility-only, specular-only, and joint variants trade 90% interval coverage against width on mixed versus pure rays?
Use a diffusion geometry prior with visibility masks and a specular likelihood; conformalize occluded and reflective depth intervals separately.
Train visibility-masked diffusion with a specular likelihood; conformalize by region and compare held-out coverage and width against error-matched ensembles.
Use the MirrorOcclude-3V ablation report’s ray strata to test conformalized diffusion intervals against error-matched ensembles on occluded and reflective regions.
DiffusionBench-v1 report tabulating regional 90% depth coverage and interval width versus error-matched ensembles across MirrorOcclude-3V ray strata.
Audit DiffusionBench-v1 against reruns of VisBRDF-SDF mixture and diffusion on matched-error MirrorOcclude-3V splits; compare regional coverage and width.
DiffusionBench-v1 audit: diffusion achieved 91% occluded and 90% reflective coverage, with 27% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Select conformalized diffusion over mixture heads: regional coverage rises from 90%/88% to 91%/90%, and ensemble-relative narrowing from 23% to 27%.
Does regionwise conformal coverage remain 85–95% under unseen surface roughness and lighting, or does reflective calibration fail?
Under unseen roughness and lighting, regionwise conformalization will under-cover reflective depths (<85%) while occluded coverage remains ≥85%.
Test frozen diffusion calibrators on MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift’s unseen roughness and lighting, measuring occluded and reflective 90% depth-interval coverage.
Factorize a particle-filter posterior into visibility-driven missing-surface particles and microfacet-BRDF particles; calibrate regional depth quantiles separately.
Will particle-filter depth intervals retain coverage on reflective–occluded intersections without widening beyond calibrated ensembles?
Fit regional calibrators and run a 1,024-particle visibility/BRDF filter on MirrorOcclude-3V intersections; compare 90% coverage and width against error-matched ensembles.
MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift diffusion retained 88% reflective/90% occluded coverage; particle intersections covered 86% with 5% wider intervals than matched-error ensembles.
Across held-out mixed-ray scenes, unpruned 1,024-particle posteriors will retain 85–95% coverage but exceed matched-error ensemble width.
Evaluate unpruned 1,024-particle filtering on held-out MirrorOcclude-3V objects; measure mixed-ray 90% coverage and width versus error-matched ensembles.
On held-out MirrorOcclude-3V objects, unpruned particles covered only 82% of mixed rays; intervals were 7% wider than matched-error ensembles.
Visibility-stratified particle resampling plus mixed-ray conformal calibration will restore 85–95% coverage and shrink intervals ≥20% versus ensembles.
Implement visibility-stratified resampling and mixed-ray conformal calibration; benchmark held-out MirrorOcclude-3V coverage and width against error-matched ensembles.
Held-out MirrorOcclude-3V: stratified particles achieved 89% mixed-ray coverage with 21% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Stress-test stratified particles on MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift, measuring separate occluded/reflective coverage and ensemble-relative interval width at matched reconstruction error.
On MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift, stratified particles covered 90% occluded but 83% reflective depths; intervals narrowed only 14% versus error-matched ensembles.
Does shifted microfacet roughness corrupt reflective particle weights, explaining 83% coverage despite visibility-stratified resampling?
Roughness-shifted BRDF weights cause undercoverage; roughness marginalization should restore 85–95% reflective-intersection coverage and ≥20% narrower intervals versus ensembles.
Ablate roughness marginalization versus original stratified particles on MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift; measure reflective-intersection coverage, particle effective sample size, and ensemble-relative width.
On MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift, roughness-marginalized stratified particles achieved 89% mixed-ray coverage and 21% narrowing versus matched-error ensembles, but reflective intersections covered 82%.
Defer particles: 89% held-out mixed-ray coverage and 21% shifted mixed-ray narrowing cannot offset 83% shifted reflective or 82% intersection coverage.
Does multi-bounce reflection, rather than roughness mismatch, explain the remaining 82% coverage at reflective–occluded intersections?
Unmodeled second-bounce specular paths cause intersection undercoverage; adding two-bounce likelihoods will raise intersection coverage from 82% to ≥85%.
Re-evaluate n36/n40 shifted failure rays with two-bounce likelihoods versus roughness-marginalized particles; measure reflective-intersection coverage and interval width.
On MirrorOcclude-3V-Shift, two-bounce likelihoods raised reflective-intersection coverage from 82% to 88%, with intervals 19% narrower than ensembles.
Retain particle deferral: two-bounce repairs intersection coverage to 88%, but 19% narrowing falls short locally; prioritize selected diffusion.
Train a ray-causal normalizing flow with explicit occlusion and specular-path latents, then conformalize depth intervals by visibility class.
Train ray-causal flow with two-bounce path latents; calibrate occluded and reflective depths, then benchmark coverage and width against matched-error ensembles.
Using DiffusionBench-v1’s matched-error splits and ensemble baselines, train and calibrate two-bounce ray-causal flow; measure regional coverage and interval width.
FlowBench-v1 report with calibrated occluded/reflective depth coverage and mean interval width versus matched-error ensembles on DiffusionBench-v1 splits.
Audit FlowBench-v1 by rerunning flow and diffusion on matched splits; compare regional 90% depth coverage and ensemble-relative interval width.
FlowBench-v1 audit: ray-causal flow achieved 92% occluded and 91% reflective coverage, with 30% narrower intervals than matched-error ensembles.
Select ray-causal flow over diffusion: regional coverage improves from 91%/90% to 92%/91%, and ensemble-relative narrowing from 27% to 30%.
Fit sparse Gaussian-process SDFs with visibility-conditioned priors and highlight-motion likelihoods; conformalize occluded and reflective depths separately.
Train visibility-conditioned GP-SDFs on sparse views, calibrate regionwise depths, and compare coverage and width against error-matched ensembles.
Using FlowBench-v1 matched splits and baselines, fit GP-SDFs with highlight-motion likelihoods; measure regional 90% coverage and interval width.
GPSDFBench-v1 report listing occluded/reflective 90% depth coverage and ensemble-relative interval width on FlowBench-v1 matched splits.
Audit GPSDFBench-v1 against ray-causal flow reruns on matched-error splits, comparing regional 90% coverage and ensemble-relative mean interval width.
GPSDFBench-v1 audit: GP-SDF achieved 90% occluded and 89% reflective coverage, with intervals 22% narrower than matched-error ensembles.
Retain ray-causal flow: 30% narrowing exceeds GP-SDF’s 22%, diffusion’s 27%, and mixture heads’ 23%; particles remain deferred.
